text.t: Aquaporin 1 is a channel that lets water cross the cell membrane, which otherwise resists water.
The real channel is four identical chains, each with its own pore; this file holds one of them, from a cow.
Six helices cross the membrane, the frame that holds the water pore.
Two short loops dip into the membrane, each carrying the signature asparagine, proline, alanine (NPA).
Their two asparagines hold the central water in a fixed direction, so the channel cannot pass protons along a chain of water.
Histidine 182 lines the tightest part of the pore.
It is found in every known water-only channel and helps make sure that only water gets through.
Water molecules pass through the long, narrow pore one at a time, in single file.

does.t: Aquaporins let water flow in and out of cells that need to move a lot of water, such as in the kidneys and the eye.
In the kidney, aquaporins let water leave the tubules and return to the body, which reduces the amount of urine.

shape.t: The pore has a wide entrance on each side of the membrane, joined by a long, narrow filter.
The filter is mostly water-repelling with just a few spots that bind water, a mix that lets water rush through quickly.
Water molecules in the channel are forced to point in set directions, which blocks protons from hopping through.

text.t: This aquaporin, AQP1, is found in the membrane of red blood cells.
Kidney tubule cells also use aquaporins to take water back from the filtrate.

wrong.t: Aquaporins were first noticed because mercury blocks water flow in and out of red blood cells, but mercury is far too toxic to use as a drug.
Scientists are searching for safer aquaporin blockers to treat water-related diseases such as glaucoma.

history.who: H. Sui, B.G. Han, J.K. Lee, P. Walian and B.K. Jap

text.t: This X-ray structure of cow AQP1 at 2.2 angstroms showed how the channel lets water through but not protons.
In 2001, mammals were known to have ten families of these water channels, named AQP0 to AQP9.

compare.t: One aquaporin chain measures about 7 nm from end to end in this file.
A water molecule measures about 0.16 nm across, so the water passing through is tiny next to its channel.
